Describe associations between diseases

Source: R/inputs.R
cm_associations.Rd

Each row is one estimate from a study: an association between two diseases, or between combinations of diseases, possibly within a subgroup or adjusted for other diseases. Several rows can describe the same association (they are pooled). Pairs that no row mentions are unknown: the model fills in their association from the others (see deconflate()). To state that two diseases are unrelated, give the pair an odds ratio of 1.

Usage

cm_associations(
  disease,
  associated_with = NA_character_,
  value,
  measure = "OR",
  ...,
  among = NA_character_,
  adjusted_for = NA_character_,
  study = NA_character_,
  source = NA_character_,
  note = NA_character_
)

Arguments

disease, associated_with

Disease ids or combinations ("a;b").

value

Numeric association values (required).

measure

Character, one per row or recycled (see What a row means).

...

Not used (arguments of earlier versions give a message). The arguments after it must be named.

among

Optional subgroups (see What a row means).

adjusted_for

Optional adjustment sets (see What a row means).

study, source, note

Optional study label (used in diagnostics), citation and free-text note.

Value

A cm_associations data frame (with the row number of each row in column row).

What a row means

disease (G) is the outcome and associated_with (H) the comparison: animals with all of H against animals with none of H (for one disease, with against without). Each can be one disease or a combination, with ids separated by ";" (e.g. "MAS;SCK"). among narrows the population to a subgroup: ids that are present ("SCK"), absent ("no SCK"), both ("SCK;no MET"), or "no others" (none of the diseases not named in the row).

  • "OR" (default), "RR", "RD", "phi": odds ratio, risk ratio P(G | H) / P(G | no H), risk difference and phi correlation of the 2x2 table of G by H, within among.

  • "prevalence": P(G | H) within among; without associated_with, the prevalence of G (a combination, or a disease within a subgroup). The prevalence of one disease in the whole population belongs in cm_diseases().

  • "OR_ratio": the odds ratio of G and H among among divided by their odds ratio among the complement of among (one disease, present or absent): how much a third disease changes an association, as a study that reports stratum-specific odds ratios would give it.

adjusted_for: an odds ratio adjusted for other diseases of the model (ids separated by ";", or "all" for every other disease), from a logistic regression of G on H and those diseases, is an exact conditional association and is used as such (G and H must be single diseases). Names that are not diseases of the model (e.g. "parity") are factors outside the model: they are ignored, with a note, and a row adjusted only for them is used as a crude association.

Measures are applied to the modelled population's own probabilities ("transported"): this assumes the measure is the same in the source study and in the modelled population.

Examples

cm_associations(c("d1", "d2"), c("d2", "d3"), c(2, 3))
#>   row disease associated_with among adjusted_for measure value study source
#> 1   1      d1              d2  <NA>         <NA>      OR     2  <NA>   <NA>
#> 2   2      d2              d3  <NA>         <NA>      OR     3  <NA>   <NA>
#>   note
#> 1 <NA>
#> 2 <NA>
# An odds ratio within a subgroup, and how much d3 changes it
cm_associations(c("d1", "d1"), c("d2", "d2"), c(2.5, 1.8),
                measure = c("OR", "OR_ratio"), among = c("d3", "d3"))
#>   row disease associated_with among adjusted_for  measure value study source
#> 1   1      d1              d2    d3         <NA>       OR   2.5  <NA>   <NA>
#> 2   2      d1              d2    d3         <NA> OR_ratio   1.8  <NA>   <NA>
#>   note
#> 1 <NA>
#> 2 <NA>
